papers.title: MultiTargetDB: a comprehensive database of multitarget ligands for polypharmacology research and drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Multitarget drug discovery has gained considerable traction in recent years, particularly for the treatment of complex diseases. Despite the growing demand for dedicated, well-curated resources to advance polypharmacology research and rational multitarget drug discovery, such resources remain severely limited. Here, we present MultiTargetDB, a database of multitarget ligands integrated with comprehensive biological annotations and measurement-level provenance. At the small molecule level, MultiTargetDB integrates chemical structures (including molecular scaffolds), their drug development stage
papers.summary: MultiTargetDB is a new curated database of multitarget ligands designed to support polypharmacology research and rational multitarget drug discovery. It integrates chemical structures and scaffolds with comprehensive biological annotations and measurement-level provenance, addressing the shortage of dedicated resources for this area. The database aims to help researchers identify compounds that act on multiple targets, which is especially relevant for complex diseases.

papers.title: Computational network pharmacology and molecular simulations to explore the potential mechanisms of Pyrrosia piloselloides compounds against prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer is major cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality in men worldwide. Emerging evidence highlights the dragon scale fern (Pyrrosia piloselloides or P. piloselloides) has demonstrated anticancer potential, but its molecular mechanisms against prostate cancer remain unclear. The study aimed to investigate its potential anticancer compounds and underlying molecular mechanisms using an integrated in silico approach.
papers.journal: Journal of the Egyptian National Cancer Institute
papers.summary: This study uses computational network pharmacology and molecular simulation to predict which compounds in the dragon scale fern (Pyrrosia piloselloides) might act against prostate cancer and through which molecular targets. It is a purely in silico analysis, so the findings are hypotheses about potential mechanisms rather than experimentally validated results.

papers.title: From LC-MS Metabolomic Profiling to AIEnabled Navigation of NPs Chemical Space: Recent Advances and Emerging Directions.
papers.abstract: Natural products (NPs) occupy a unique region of chemical space and continue to provide privileged scaffolds for drug discovery, chemical ecology, and biotechnology. However, the exploration of NP diversity remains constrained by the complexity of biological extracts, the low annotation rate of LC-MS features, and the rediscovery of known metabolites. Recent advances in LC-HRMS/MS-based metabolomics, coupled with expanding spectral and structural databases, molecular networking, and in silico annotation methods, have considerably improved the characterization of complex metabolomes and facilit
papers.summary: This review discusses how LC-MS metabolomic profiling, combined with expanding spectral databases, molecular networking, and in silico annotation, is improving the characterization of complex natural product extracts. It highlights how AI-enabled navigation of natural product chemical space can help overcome low annotation rates and rediscovery of known metabolites, accelerating natural product-based drug discovery and biotechnology.

papers.title: Modeling ethnic differences via drug-predicted clearance from chemical structures.
papers.abstract: Ethnic differences in pharmacokinetics can result in clinically relevant differences in drug efficacy and safety, even when identical doses are administered. Although mechanistic approaches such as physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling can be used to evaluate population-specific pharmacokinetics, there remains a need for complementary screening approaches that can assess ethnic difference risk at very early stages of drug discovery with limited experimental information. The aim of this study was to develop a machine-learning-based approach to assess the risk of ethnic differences in o
papers.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
papers.summary: This study develops a machine-learning approach that predicts drug clearance directly from chemical structures to flag the risk of ethnic differences in pharmacokinetics early in drug discovery. The method offers a fast, complementary screening tool to resource-intensive physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling when experimental data are limited.

papers.title: DockBind: A Quality-Controlled Data Set of Modeled Protein-Ligand Complexes Associated with Affinity Data.
papers.abstract: Ligand-protein interaction prediction is essential for structure-based drug discovery, but further development of machine-learning scoring functions is limited by a lack of high-quality training data sets. Here, we present DockBind, a curated data set of modeled protein-ligand complexes paired with experimental binding affinity data, generated through a quality-controlled docking workflow. This workflow was developed based on an expanded docking benchmark, where we systematically evaluated free and template-based docking methods as well as ligand similarity and maximum common substructure (MCS
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: DockBind is a new curated dataset of modeled protein-ligand complexes paired with experimental binding affinity data, built through a quality-controlled docking workflow. The authors systematically benchmarked free and template-based docking methods, along with ligand similarity and maximum common substructure approaches, to ensure high-quality complex models. This resource aims to address the shortage of high-quality training data that limits the development of machine-learning scoring functions for structure-based drug discovery.

papers.title: Evaluation of Physics-Based Pose Prediction and the Role of Receptor Flexibility in a Community Antiviral Blind Challenge.
papers.abstract: Prediction of protein-ligand binding modes is a key step in computer-aided drug design, since incorrect pose prediction inevitably limits the achievable accuracy of downstream physics-based affinity predictions. The ASAP-Polaris-OpenADMET antiviral competition was launched in 2025 as a means to prospectively test computational methods across a range of measurements that guide early prioritization during a drug discovery campaign including pose prediction. Here, we describe our two open-source, physics-based entries to the pose prediction challenge, which are based on templated molecular growth
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This paper reports on two open-source, physics-based methods for predicting how small antiviral molecules bind to their protein targets, submitted to the 2025 ASAP-Polaris-OpenADMET blind challenge. The methods use templated molecular growth and explicitly account for receptor flexibility, and the authors evaluate their performance against other community entries. The work highlights both the promise and current limitations of physics-based pose prediction in realistic drug-discovery settings.

papers.title: Structure-function relationships in a square-planar Cu(ii) hybrid halometalate: experimental, DFT, molecular docking, optical, and biological studies.
papers.abstract: A novel organic-inorganic copper(ii) hybrid halometalate, (C6H8BrN2)2[CuBr4], was successfully synthesized and investigated using complementary experimental and computational approaches. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis revealed discrete square-planar [CuBr4]2- anions embedded within a three-dimensional supramolecular architecture stabilized by N-H⋯Br hydrogen bonds, π-π stacking interactions, and halogen contacts. Optical studies indicated semiconducting characteristics with an estimated band gap of approximately 2.5 eV, together with a broad visible emission assigned to ligand-to-me
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a new organic-inorganic copper(II) hybrid halometalate, (C6H8BrN2)2[CuBr4], and characterized it with X-ray crystallography, optical spectroscopy, DFT calculations, molecular docking, and biological assays. The material features discrete square-planar [CuBr4]2- anions in a supramolecular framework held together by hydrogen bonds, π-π stacking, and halogen contacts, and shows semiconducting behavior with a ~2.5 eV band gap plus broad visible emission. The study links the crystal structure to optical and biological properties.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in myeloproliferative neoplasms: From digital bone marrow pathology to clinical decision support.
papers.abstract: Myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN) are clonal hematopoietic stem cell disorders whose diagnosis, prognostication, and management depend on integrating heterogeneous clinical, morphological, and molecular data. This narrative review (PubMed/MEDLINE searched through August 2026, supplemented by hand-searching and conference abstracts) appraises the evidence for AI applications across the MPN continuum. Artificial intelligence (AI), and its principal subfields, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), learn predictive patterns directly from data rather than from explicitly programmed rules,
papers.summary: This narrative review surveys the evidence for artificial intelligence applications across the myeloproliferative neoplasm (MPN) continuum, from digital bone marrow pathology to clinical decision support. It examines how machine learning and deep learning can integrate heterogeneous clinical, morphological, and molecular data to aid diagnosis, prognostication, and management. The review appraises the current state of the field and likely identifies gaps and future directions for AI in MPN care.

papers.title: Innovative design and development of novel thiazole-paracetamol hybrids as COX inhibitors and immunomodulatory activity: design, synthesis, SAR, in vitro biological evaluation, and molecular docking analysis.
papers.abstract: The hybridization approach was employed to design a single pharmacophore based on the conjugation of paracetamol with thiazole derivatives, yielding thiazole-paracetamol hybrid derivatives 4-11 that utilize a linker from hydrazone (-C[double bond, length as m-dash]N-NH) and azo (-N[double bond, length as m-dash]N-) linkers, serving as the hydrogen bond donor/acceptor binding site. The structure of the designed derivatives was fully characterized and confirmed using analytical data (IR, 1H NMR, and 13C NMR), and elemental analysis. The anti-inflammatory potential of the synthesized hybrids was
papers.summary: This paper reports the design and synthesis of hybrid molecules that combine paracetamol with thiazole derivatives via hydrazone or azo linkers, aiming to create dual-acting COX inhibitors with immunomodulatory activity. The compounds were characterized spectroscopically and evaluated in vitro for anti-inflammatory potential, with structure-activity relationships and molecular docking supporting the design rationale.

papers.title: Integrative network pharmacology and experimental evaluation reveal TNBC-related biological activity and toxicity of Euphorbia umbellata crude latex.
papers.abstract: Euphorbia umbellata latex is used in Brazilian traditional medicine, including empirically for cancer treatment. However, its chemical composition, molecular targets, pharmacological properties, and biological effects in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remain insufficiently characterized. This study investigated the TNBC-related biological activity and toxicity of E. umbellata crude latex by integrating computational analyses with experimental evaluation in a 4T1 cell model. Eighteen compounds previously identified in E. umbellata crude latex were curated from phytochemical studies and ev
papers.summary: This study combined computational network pharmacology with experimental testing in 4T1 triple-negative breast cancer cells to characterize the anti-cancer activity and toxicity of Euphorbia umbellata crude latex, a plant used in Brazilian traditional medicine. The authors curated 18 known latex compounds and mapped them to predicted molecular targets and pathways relevant to TNBC, then validated key effects experimentally. The work provides an initial integrative profile of the latex's pharmacological potential and safety concerns in a TNBC context.

papers.title: In Silico Investigation of Candidate Anticancer Targets for Aryltetralin Lignans Previously Reported from Cleistanthus Species.
papers.abstract: Aryltetralin lignans isolated from the fruits of Cleistanthus species exhibit substantial cytotoxic activity, although the molecular interactions underlying these effects remain incompletely understood. This study combined computational target investigation with previously published experimental chemical characterization and cytotoxic evidence and no new isolation or cytotoxicity experiments were carried out. Cleistantoxin, 7-hydroxypicropolygamain, neo-cleistantoxin, cleisindoside A, cleisindoside D, and cleistonkinin D were previously isolated from C. indochinensis, C. tonkinensis, C. eberha
papers.summary: This study used computational docking and target-prediction approaches to investigate which protein targets might explain the anticancer activity of aryltetralin lignans previously isolated from Cleistanthus species. No new compounds were isolated and no new experiments were performed; the work integrates prior chemical and cytotoxicity data with in silico target predictions. The findings propose candidate anticancer targets for these natural products, offering hypotheses for future experimental validation.

papers.title: Xanthine oxidase inhibitory evaluation of prenylated flavonoids from peanut (Arachis hypogaea L.) shells: in vitro and in silico molecular docking studies.
papers.abstract: Sustainable agriculture has become a crucial priority because the improper management of agricultural waste currently contributes to greenhouse gas emissions, as well as soil and air pollution. The shells of Arachis hypogaea L., which is commonly discarded as an agricultural by-product, have been reported to contain various secondary metabolites, including flavonoids, stilbenes, triterpenoids, etc. This work led to the isolation of two new prenylated flavonoids, arachisflavones A (1) and B (2), together with five prenylated flavones (3-7), two prenylated chalcones (8-9), and three prenylated f
papers.summary: This study isolated two new prenylated flavonoids (arachisflavones A and B) along with several known prenylated flavones and chalcones from peanut shells, an agricultural waste product. The compounds were evaluated for xanthine oxidase inhibition in vitro and via molecular docking, identifying peanut shell flavonoids as potential natural xanthine oxidase inhibitors. The work highlights a sustainable use for peanut shell waste as a source of bioactive compounds.

papers.title: Rational design and synthesis of furan-based Schiff base quinazolin-4-amine hybrids: spectral elucidation, molecular docking, DFT studies, and in silico ADMET-antioxidant study.
papers.abstract: In this work, a new series of furan-based quinazoline-4-amine hydrazone (Schiff base) derivatives (4a-h) was rationally designed and synthesized in good yields (84-90%) through a multistep route involving nucleophilic aromatic substitution, Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling, and hydrazone/Schiff base condensation reactions. The synthesized compounds were characterized by FT-IR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and ESI-mass spectrometry, which confirmed the proposed structures. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed to optimize the molecular geometries and to derive frontier molecular orbital
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a series of eight furan-based quinazoline-4-amine Schiff base hybrids (4a-h) using a multistep route combining nucleophilic aromatic substitution, Suzuki-Miyaura coupling, and hydrazone condensation, achieving 84-90% yields. Compounds were structurally confirmed by FT-IR, NMR, and mass spectrometry, and evaluated computationally via DFT, molecular docking, and in silico ADMET/antioxidant predictions. The work is a medicinal chemistry design/synthesis study with only computational (not experimental) biological evaluation.

papers.title: NU-1025 modulates immunogenic cell death in bladder cancer: A multi-omics insight.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade has shown limited efficacy in bladder cancer, underscoring the need for therapeutic strategies that enhance tumor immunogenicity. Immunogenic cell death (ICD) can stimulate adaptive immunity and remodel the tumor microenvironment, yet its comprehensive landscape and druggable potential in bladder cancer remain unexplored. Here, we performed integrative bioinformatics analysis of transcriptomic data from TCGA and GEO bladder cancer cohorts to characterize ICD-associated subtypes, construct a prognostic risk model, and analyze immune infiltration. Connectivity Map (CMa
papers.summary: This study used multi-omics bioinformatics to characterize immunogenic cell death (ICD) patterns in bladder cancer, identifying ICD-associated subtypes and building a prognostic risk model from TCGA and GEO transcriptomic data. The authors then used Connectivity Map analysis to nominate NU-1025 as a compound that modulates ICD and may enhance tumor immunogenicity, offering a potential strategy to improve immune checkpoint blockade response.

papers.title: A Pathway-Driven Computational Drug Discovery Framework Integrating Machine Learning and Virtual Screening for Identification of Anti-Rheumatoid Arthritis Natural Small Molecules.
papers.abstract: Objective: This study aimed to establish a pathway-driven computational drug discovery framework integrating machine learning, target prioritization, virtual screening, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and in vitro evaluation to identify natural small molecules with potential anti-rheumatoid arthritis (RA) activity. Methods: Sixteen RA-related Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets were included, with 15 cohorts used for model development and one reserved for independent external validation. Pathway features quantified by gene set variation analysis (GSVA) were subjected to cohort-aware fe
papers.summary: This study builds a computational drug discovery pipeline that combines machine learning on pathway-level features from 16 rheumatoid arthritis GEO datasets with target prioritization, virtual screening, molecular dynamics simulations, and in vitro testing to identify natural small molecules with potential anti-RA activity. The framework uses GSVA-derived pathway features for model development and reserves one cohort for independent external validation.

papers.title: Computational Identification of GABA-A Receptor Ligands Targeting the Histamine Allosteric Pocket.
papers.abstract: The γ-aminobutyric acid type A (GABA-A) receptor is a key regulator of inhibitory neurotransmission in the central nervous system, and a promising target for cognitive and neurological disorders. Histamine interacts with a distinct allosteric pocket located at the β3-β3 subunit interface, providing an opportunity for the discovery of novel ligands. In the present study, an integrated in silico workflow combining ligand-based similarity analysis, ADMET filtering, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations was applied to identify candidate ligands for this histamine-associated site. D
papers.summary: This study used a computational pipeline—ligand similarity screening, ADMET filtering, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations—to search for small molecules that bind the histamine allosteric pocket at the β3-β3 interface of the GABA-A receptor. The work nominates candidate ligands for this site as a starting point for developing compounds aimed at cognitive and neurological disorders. Findings are purely in silico and require experimental validation.

papers.title: Navigating the Eukaryotic Paradox: Insights for AI-Driven Computational Strategies Against Antifungal Resistance.
papers.abstract: The escalating crisis of invasive fungal infections and increasing antifungal resistance demand rapid therapeutic innovation. Given the critically narrow clinical arsenal, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have emerged as pivotal strategies to accelerate drug repurposing, providing a rapid alternative to de novo drug discovery. However, translational success in medical mycology faces a major biological hurdle: the "eukaryotic paradox," the extensive genomic, metabolic, and structural homology between fungal cells and human hosts. This review provides a critical and compara
papers.summary: This review examines how the close biological similarity between fungal pathogens and human cells—the 'eukaryotic paradox'—complicates AI-driven drug repurposing for antifungal resistance. It surveys computational strategies and highlights the need to account for host-pathogen homology when prioritizing candidate compounds.

papers.title: From Mechanistic Models to AI Synergy: A Roadmap for Predictive and Personalized Biology.
papers.abstract: Two paradigms now drive the life sciences. One is the explanatory depth of mathematical modeling, the other the predictive power of artificial intelligence. For decades, mechanistic models have offered a rigorous, hypothesis-driven framework for dissecting biological processes, while AI has proven itself at finding patterns in the large, high-dimensional datasets of modern biology. Each has delivered major advances on its own. Together they promise a synthesis that could redefine the boundaries of biological inquiry. In this review we propose a three-part taxonomy of integration strategies, na
papers.summary: This review proposes a three-part taxonomy for integrating mechanistic mathematical models with artificial intelligence in the life sciences, arguing that the explanatory depth of mechanistic modeling and the pattern-finding power of AI are complementary rather than competing paradigms. The authors outline a roadmap toward predictive and personalized biology built on this synthesis. The paper is a conceptual and organizational contribution rather than a new empirical result.

papers.title: QSAR-Guided In Silico Design of Piperazinylanthranilamide Factor Xa Inhibitors: Applicability-Domain Assessment, ADMET Profiling, Molecular Docking, Molecular Dynamics, and MM/GBSA.
papers.abstract: An integrated computational workflow was developed to prioritize piperazinylanthranilamide factor Xa (FXa) inhibitor candidates. Twenty literature compounds were geometry-optimized and described using alvaDesc to construct a constrained additive multivariate adaptive regression splines model. Internal validation and an assessment of the applicability domain guided the evaluation of 20 prospective analogs. Ten selected analogs and two same-series references were docked to FXa, with apixaban as the crystallographic comparator. Thirteen initial 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations were supplemen
papers.summary: This study uses a computational workflow combining QSAR modeling, applicability-domain assessment, ADMET profiling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics, and MM/GBSA to prioritize piperazinylanthranilamide analogs as factor Xa inhibitors. Twenty literature compounds were used to build a constrained additive MARS model, which guided the selection of ten prospective analogs for docking and simulation against apixaban. The work demonstrates an integrated in silico pipeline for early-stage inhibitor design, though experimental validation is absent.

papers.title: Donor-Resolved Analysis of HES1-Associated Fibroblast States in Systemic Sclerosis.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: We examined HES1-associated fibroblast states in systemic sclerosis (SSc) and the rationale for testing upstream γ-secretase inhibition with nirogacestat. Methods: We analysed 325,636 skin cells from 230 donors across five non-redundant cohorts using complete computational transcription-factor screens, donor-level activity and trajectory analyses, multiome data and spatial assays. Donors or independent simulations were the inference units, with cohort adjustment and multiplicity correction where applicable. Three independent 200 ns molecular dynamics runs per condition c
papers.summary: This study analyzed over 325,000 skin cells from 230 donors across five cohorts to characterize HES1-associated fibroblast states in systemic sclerosis (SSc). The authors used transcription-factor screens, donor-level activity and trajectory analyses, multiome and spatial data, and molecular dynamics simulations to build a rationale for testing upstream γ-secretase inhibition with nirogacestat. The work highlights donor-resolved fibroblast heterogeneity and proposes a candidate therapeutic strategy for SSc.

papers.title: The Application of Artificial Intelligence in Brucellosis: Diagnosis, Genomic Analysis, Epidemiological Prediction and Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Brucellosis, a globally significant zoonosis caused by Brucella, poses a substantial impediment to the sustainable development of the livestock industry and threatens public health security. Traditional control and prevention strategies for brucellosis suffer from fundamental limitations. These include the time-consuming, biosafety risks associated with bacterial culture and the difficulty in differentiating between natural infection and vaccine-induced immunity with serological tests. There remains a challenge in accurately distinguishing vaccine strains from wild-type strains via genotyping
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence is being applied across four areas of brucellosis research: diagnosis, genomic analysis, epidemiological forecasting, and drug discovery. It highlights that traditional control strategies are limited by slow and biosafety-risky culture methods, difficulty distinguishing natural infection from vaccine-induced immunity in serology, and challenges in separating vaccine from wild-type strains via genotyping, and argues AI can help address these gaps. As a review, it synthesizes existing approaches rather than presenting new experimental results.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Guided Virtual Screening Identifies a Novel MELK-Targeted Antiproliferative Lead Compound with G2/M Arrest Activity in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer and Lung Adenocarcinoma Cells.
papers.abstract: Background: Maternal embryonic leucine zipper kinase (MELK) is a cell cycle-regulated serine/threonine kinase frequently overexpressed in human malignancies, and represents a promising anticancer drug target. Discovery of structurally novel, highly selective MELK inhibitors remains an unmet need. Methods: In the study, we implemented an integrated computational pipeline combining four machine learning regressors (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, LightGBM), hierarchical Glide docking (HTVS to SP to XP), MM/GBSA rescoring, ADMET prediction, and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations to
papers.summary: This study used an integrated computational pipeline—combining machine learning regressors, hierarchical molecular docking, MM/GBSA rescoring, ADMET prediction, and molecular dynamics simulations—to virtually screen for novel inhibitors of the kinase MELK, a cancer target overexpressed in several malignancies. The screen identified a lead compound that showed antiproliferative activity and induced G2/M cell cycle arrest in triple-negative breast cancer and lung adenocarcinoma cell lines. The work presents a machine learning-guided virtual screening strategy for discovering structurally novel kinase inhibitors.

papers.title: Identifying Anticancer Peptide via a Semi-Supervised Prediction Framework with Bio-Inspired Augmentation.
papers.abstract: Anticancer peptides (ACPs) have emerged as a promising class of therapeutic molecules due to their low toxicity and high specificity. However, experimentally identifying ACPs is labor-intensive and low-throughput, making virtual screening with intelligent models an attractive alternative. Despite recent progress, the number of ACP samples available in existing databases remains limited, which may cause predictive models to overfit the labeled information and exhibit suboptimal generalization. To address this issue, we propose a semi-supervised prediction framework with bio-inspired data augmen
papers.summary: The authors propose a semi-supervised framework for predicting anticancer peptides that uses bio-inspired data augmentation to compensate for the limited size of labeled ACP datasets. This approach aims to reduce overfitting and improve generalization compared to models trained only on the scarce labeled data. The work is a methodological contribution to computational peptide screening rather than a new biological finding.

papers.title: Network Pharmacology of Natural Products from Computational Prediction to Experimental Validation.
papers.abstract: Natural products are important sources of bioactive compounds, but their complex chemical composition and multi-target effects make their mechanisms difficult to investigate using conventional approaches. Network pharmacology provides a systems-level framework for integrating chemical, biological, and disease-related information to investigate these complex interactions. This review describes the network pharmacology workflow, from active-compound screening, ADMET evaluation and target prediction to network construction and pathway enrichment, and the complementary roles of molecular docking a
papers.summary: This review describes the network pharmacology workflow for studying natural products, covering active-compound screening, ADMET evaluation, target prediction, network construction, and pathway enrichment, along with complementary molecular docking and experimental validation. It provides a systems-level framework for investigating the multi-target mechanisms of complex natural product mixtures.

papers.title: A Computational Workflow Integrating Explainable AI and Database Mining for the Prioritization of Antimicrobial Natural Products.
papers.abstract: The escalating threat of antimicrobial resistance demands the discovery of antibacterial agents with unprecedented chemical scaffolds. Natural products have historically been the most prolific source of antibiotics, yet the vast majority of catalogued natural products remain untested for antimicrobial activity. Here we present Natural-Product Graph-language, Uncertainty-Aware Relational Discovery (NP-GUARD), a modular computational framework that reframes antimicrobial natural-product discovery as an uncertainty-aware, relational, multi-objective learning problem. NP-GUARD integrates six core
papers.summary: The authors present NP-GUARD, a modular computational framework that combines explainable AI with database mining to prioritize natural products with potential antimicrobial activity. It frames antimicrobial natural-product discovery as an uncertainty-aware, relational, multi-objective learning problem, integrating six core components to help triage the vast untested natural-product space. The work aims to accelerate identification of antibacterial candidates with novel chemical scaffolds.

papers.title: Advancing the Translational Pipeline: From In Vivo and In Vitro 2D Models to Next-Generation Cell Culture Models for Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Modelling and Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Background: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is still a global health challenge, as there is no effective treatment due to the inadequacy of conventional experimental platforms for comprehending pathogenic mechanisms and developing therapy. Objectives: This review details the recent progress and clinical utility of next-generation iPSC-derived 3D in vitro systems integrated with microfluidics, CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, multi-omics readouts, and AI-based machine learning, which are emerging as transformative platforms for recapitulating key ALS pathological hallmarks. Methods: A literature s
papers.summary: This review surveys next-generation ALS disease models, arguing that conventional 2D cultures and animal models are insufficient for understanding pathogenesis and developing treatments. It highlights iPSC-derived 3D systems combined with microfluidics, CRISPR-Cas9 editing, multi-omics, and AI/machine learning as transformative platforms that better recapitulate ALS hallmarks for drug discovery.

papers.title: DeepAVPred: A Deep Learning Framework Integrating RECM-DWT and BiGRU for Accurate Antiviral Peptide Prediction.
papers.abstract: Viral infections continue to pose a significant global health challenge. Antiviral peptides (AVPs) have emerged as promising therapeutic agents owing to their high specificity, favorable safety profiles, and broad-spectrum antiviral activity. However, experimental AVP identification is time-consuming and costly, while existing computational predictors often have limitations in predictive accuracy and feature representation. Here, we propose DeepAVPred, a deep learning-based framework for AVP identification. DeepAVPred integrates complementary sequence descriptors to capture physicochemical pro
papers.summary: DeepAVPred is a deep learning framework for identifying antiviral peptides from sequence data, combining a novel residue-level encoding method (RECM-DWT) with a bidirectional GRU network. The approach aims to improve on existing computational predictors that struggle with accuracy and feature representation, offering a faster alternative to costly experimental screening. It is a specialized tool for antiviral peptide discovery.

papers.title: In Silico Discovery of a Potential PI3Kα Inhibitor Incorporating an Imidazole Moiety for Breast Cancer Treatment.
papers.abstract: Excessive activation of PI3Kα is prevalent in breast cancer, aberrantly activating the PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway to drive tumor progression, thus rendering PI3Kα a vital therapeutic target. Two PI3Kα inhibitors (alpelisib and inavolisib) have been approved for clinical application. Inavolisib exerts a mutation-selective degradation mechanism and functions by directly eliminating aberrant proteins. To develop novel PI3Kα inhibitors, we employed multiple computational strategies including scaffold hopping based on the structure of inavolisib, -CDOCKER docking, Lipinski's rule of five, ADMET predicti
papers.summary: The authors used computational methods—scaffold hopping from the approved PI3Kα inhibitor inavolisib, molecular docking, Lipinski rule-of-five filtering, and ADMET prediction—to identify a novel imidazole-containing compound as a potential PI3Kα inhibitor for breast cancer. This is a purely in silico study with no experimental validation, so the candidate remains hypothetical until tested in vitro and in vivo.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Driven Identification and Experimental Validation of COX-2 and ERK1/2 as Anti-Inflammatory Targets of Avenanthramides.
papers.abstract: Chronic low-grade inflammation underlies numerous chronic diseases, yet the molecular targets of dietary bioactive compounds remain largely unknown.
papers.summary: This study uses deep learning to predict molecular targets of avenanthramides, oat-derived polyphenols with anti-inflammatory properties, and identifies COX-2 and ERK1/2 as key targets. Experimental validation confirms that avenanthramides inhibit these proteins, providing a mechanistic basis for their anti-inflammatory effects. The work demonstrates how computational target prediction can guide the discovery of dietary bioactive compound mechanisms.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics-Guided Triage of Approved Drugs Against Escherichia coli Resistance Targets Nominates Capmatinib, Metergoline and Nilotinib as Candidates for Experimental Testing.
papers.abstract: Virtual screening ranks compounds by scoring functions that correlate with molecular size, and hit lists are rarely benchmarked against compounds of established activity. We screened 2070 approved drugs against four Escherichia coli targets selected by pocket-druggability triage (FabI, LpxC, DHFR and GyrB), with each docking protocol validated by redocking its native ligand (RMSD 0.50-0.69 Å). Per target, the two top-scoring compounds and a reference inhibitor were simulated for 100 ns in triplicate (12 complexes, 3.6 μs). Docking did not recover the references: trimethoprim ranked 762/2068 an
papers.summary: The authors docked 2070 approved drugs against four E. coli antibacterial targets and then used 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations to triage top hits, nominating capmatinib, metergoline, and nilotinib for experimental testing. Notably, docking failed to recover known reference inhibitors (e.g., trimethoprim ranked 762nd), highlighting a key limitation of scoring-function-based virtual screening and the value of MD-based refinement.

papers.title: Language of Toxicity: An eXplainable Artificial Intelligence Approach.
papers.abstract: Toxicity prediction in small molecules represents a fundamental challenge in drug development and chemical safety assessment. Traditional approaches heavily rely on predefined molecular descriptors or fingerprints, potentially limiting the ability to capture complex and nonlinear structure-activity relationships. Here, we present a descriptor-free, language-inspired framework that can be applied to different toxicity prediction tasks within a unified architecture. The model proposed combines a multiscale Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) layer to capture chemical patterns at different scales
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: The authors present a descriptor-free, language-inspired deep learning framework for predicting small-molecule toxicity. It uses a multiscale CNN to capture chemical patterns at different scales within a unified architecture applicable to multiple toxicity prediction tasks, aiming to overcome limitations of predefined molecular descriptors and fingerprints.

papers.title: Senescence-Associated Transcriptome Reversal Prioritizes Repurposing Candidates for Diabetic Kidney Disease: A Computational Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a leading cause of end-stage kidney disease, and cellular senescence is a tractable therapeutic target; yet prioritizing credible repurposing candidates is difficult because bulk-tissue senescence signals are weak, single-dataset analyses are unstable, and transcriptome-reversal screens overstate novelty. The objective was to build a senescence-anchored, multi-evidence computational prioritization of repurposing candidates for DKD entirely from open data. Methods: Per-sample senescence activity was quantified by single-sample gene set enr
papers.summary: This computational study integrates multiple open transcriptomic datasets to build a senescence-anchored prioritization framework for drug repurposing in diabetic kidney disease. By scoring per-sample senescence activity and using transcriptome-reversal analysis combined with multi-evidence filtering, the authors identify candidate compounds that may counteract senescence-associated gene expression in DKD. The work is a hypothesis-generating in silico screen rather than an experimental validation.

papers.title: Validated Semantic Scoring Improves Filtering of Generic Concepts from Knowledge Graphs for Drug Repurposing Queries.
papers.abstract: When an ontology-based biomedical knowledge graph (a KG, containing information about genes, pathways, phenotypes, and molecular interactions) is analyzed using a computational reasoning system, the system can return unwanted generic concepts. Such generic concepts, in the context of a query about potential drug treatments for a disease, might include 'pharmaceutical preparations' or 'antibiotics'. Answers can be filtered based on hand-curated block-lists or ontology Information Content (IC), but to our knowledge, (1) neither filtering method has been validated against expert judgments of gene
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces a validated semantic scoring method to filter out overly generic concepts (like 'pharmaceutical preparations') that knowledge graph reasoning systems return when querying for drug repurposing candidates. The authors show that their semantic scoring approach outperforms existing hand-curated block-lists and ontology Information Content (IC) filtering, as validated against expert judgments. This improves the precision of ontology-based drug repurposing queries.

papers.title: Hybrid Mechanistic-Neural Modeling of Concentration-Time Dynamics Generalizes Human Pharmacokinetics Prediction Across Unseen Chemical Space.
papers.abstract: The pharmacokinetics concentration-time profile encodes ADME dynamics. Its optimization in drug discovery curbs late-stage attrition, yet forecasting human pharmacokinetics from chemical structure remains difficult. Machine learning models ignore continuous ADME dynamics, whereas physiologically based pharmacokinetics (PBPK) models demand unavailable parameters and impose rigid, misspecified compartmental structures. We present PK-MUSE (PharmacoKinetic hybrid Mechanistic Universal System Equation), augmenting a two-compartment model with bounded, state- and time-dependent neural corrections to
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present PK-MUSE, a hybrid model that augments a standard two-compartment pharmacokinetic model with neural network corrections that are bounded and depend on state and time. This approach combines the interpretability of mechanistic PBPK modeling with the flexibility of machine learning, and reportedly generalizes to predict human concentration-time profiles for chemicals outside the training space. It addresses a key drug-discovery bottleneck: forecasting human PK from structure alone without requiring unavailable physiological parameters.

papers.title: Old Drugs, New Targets: Molecular Docking Insights into Repurposing Proton Pump Inhibitors for the TLR4/MD-2, NLRP3, and C5aR1 Axes in Autoimmune Liver Diseases.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Autoimmune liver diseases (AILDs), including autoimmune hepatitis, primary biliary cholangitis, and primary sclerosing cholangitis, may include treatment-resistant cases and therefore require new therapeutic strategies. This in silico study evaluated proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) across three pathophysiologically complementary inflammatory targets relevant to hepatic immune injury: TLR4/MD-2, representing upstream innate immune sensing; NLRP3, representing inflammasome-mediated inflammatory amplification; and C5aR1, representing complement-dependent leukocyte recruitment
papers.summary: This in silico docking study tested several proton pump inhibitors against three inflammation-related protein targets (TLR4/MD-2, NLRP3, and C5aR1) implicated in autoimmune liver diseases, aiming to explore drug repurposing opportunities. The work is purely computational and reports predicted binding affinities without experimental validation, so it offers hypotheses rather than demonstrated efficacy.

papers.title: Drugging the Undruggable in Oncology: Structural Computation, Machine Learning, and Generative AI for Historically Intractable Targets.
papers.abstract: For four decades the central oncogenic drivers of human cancer the RAS GTPases, the transcription-factor MYC, mutant p53, and the protein-tyrosine phosphatases, fusion oncoproteins and intrinsically disordered regulators that surround them were regarded as undruggable: lacking deep, well-defined small-molecule binding pockets, governed by femtomolar substrate affinities, or driven through flat protein-protein interfaces that classical medicinal chemistry could not engage. The last decade has overturned that verdict. This narrative review argues that the convergence of three advances has made t
papers.summary: This narrative review argues that the long-standing view of key cancer drivers like RAS, MYC, mutant p53, and protein-tyrosine phosphatases as 'undruggable' has been overturned. It describes how structural computation, machine learning, and generative AI are converging to enable drug discovery against these historically intractable targets, such as through engaging flat protein-protein interfaces and other previously inaccessible binding modes.

papers.title: Network-Guided Drug Repurposing for Hantaan Virus Infection in Endothelial Cells: Pathway Analysis, Target Identification, and Mechanistic ODE Simulations.
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses cause haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, which are together the cause of more than 200,000 human cases every year. However, no specific antiviral therapy is approved. Here, we develop a three-stage computational framework for systematic drug repurposing. Transcriptome-wide analysis of hantavirus-infected human endothelial cells showed a response dominated by interferon pathways. A STRING protein-protein interaction network and a composite network centrality score identified 15 hub genes, including ISG15, IRF1, CXCL10, STAT1, and DDX58.
papers.summary: The authors built a three-stage computational pipeline to find existing drugs that could be repurposed against Hantaan virus, which currently has no approved antiviral therapy. Using transcriptome data from infected human endothelial cells, they found interferon signaling dominates the response and identified 15 hub genes (e.g., ISG15, IRF1, STAT1, DDX58) via protein-interaction network centrality analysis. These hubs then feed into target identification and ODE-based mechanistic simulations to nominate drug candidates.

papers.title: Primary-Tumor Transcriptomic Signatures Associated with Circulating Tumor Cells Status in Breast Cancer: From CTC-Negative Remodeling to CTC-Associated Metastatic Programs.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) play a central role in metastasis by enabling tumor dissemination through the bloodstream. However, the molecular transition from CTC-negative (CTC-) to CTC-positive (CTC+) states and their associated systemic remodeling remain poorly understood. Methods: We performed a transcriptomic comparison between CTC+, CTC-, and healthy individuals using RNA-seq data and a bioinformatics pipeline. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were subjected to functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, survival modeling, and drug pert
papers.summary: This study compared primary breast tumor transcriptomes between patients with detectable circulating tumor cells (CTC+) and those without (CTC-), using RNA-seq and bioinformatics analyses. It identified gene expression signatures and pathways that distinguish CTC-positive from CTC-negative tumors, linking CTC status to metastatic programs and survival outcomes. The work suggests that CTC status reflects underlying transcriptional remodeling in the primary tumor.

papers.title: Can AI Help Repurpose Drugs to Fight Against Antibiotic Resistance?
papers.abstract: Drug repurposing and development to meet the threat of antimicrobial resistance can be costly and time-consuming, but AI models may be able to help. In this News and Perspectives article, JMIR Correspondent Sara Novak reports on recent research training models to identify candidate drugs to treat resistant infections.
papers.summary: This news and perspectives article reports on recent efforts to use AI models to identify existing drugs that could be repurposed to treat antibiotic-resistant infections. It highlights how machine learning can accelerate and reduce the cost of drug discovery in the fight against antimicrobial resistance.

papers.title: A multimodal digital NeuroMarker platform with composite and domain-level validity for identification of mild cognitive impairment: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is a clinically heterogeneous syndrome that can represent an early manifestation of neurodegenerative disease. Diagnosis relies on assessments that are difficult to scale, leaving many individuals unidentified.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study presents a multimodal digital NeuroMarker platform that combines multiple digital assessments to identify mild cognitive impairment, reporting both composite and domain-level validity. The platform aims to provide a scalable alternative to resource-intensive clinical assessments for detecting MCI in heterogeneous populations.

papers.title: Biosynthetic Pathways and Regulation of Antibacterial Compounds From Endophytic Fungi: From Chemistry to Genomics and Biotechnology.
papers.abstract: Endophytic fungi are non-pathogenic symbionts that represent a rich source of structurally diverse bioactive secondary metabolites. However, genome-mining studies reveal that most of their biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) remain transcriptionally silent under standard laboratory conditions, leaving much of their chemical diversity unexplored. This review examines antibacterial natural products from endophytic fungi by integrating three complementary aspects: metabolite chemistry, biosynthetic pathways, and strategies for activating cryptic BGCs. Endophytic fungi produce polyketides, non-ribos
papers.summary: This review integrates the chemistry, biosynthetic pathways, and genomic regulation of antibacterial natural products from endophytic fungi. It highlights that most biosynthetic gene clusters in these fungi are silent under standard laboratory conditions, and surveys strategies for activating cryptic BGCs to access unexplored chemical diversity. The work connects metabolite chemistry with genomics and biotechnology approaches for natural product discovery.

papers.title: Interpretable Drug-Target Prediction via Geometric Alignment: A Linear Alternative to Deep Architectural Complexity.
papers.abstract: Designing selective kinase inhibitors is a multiobjective optimization problem constrained by the structural conservation of the human kinome, along with the lack of high-quality interaction data. Traditional deep learning methods often train complex neural networks directly on small datasets and fail to generalize to new chemical scaffolds. To this end, we present Geometric Manifold Alignment, a novel linear approach that shifts away from architectural complexity. We introduce Multi-View Linear Manifold (MVLM), which aligns the latent spaces of ChemBERTa (small molecules) and ESM-2 (protein s
papers.summary: The authors propose Multi-View Linear Manifold (MVLM), a linear method that aligns latent embeddings from ChemBERTa (for small molecules) and ESM-2 (for proteins) to predict kinase inhibitor–target interactions. By replacing complex deep architectures with geometric alignment, the approach aims to improve generalization to new chemical scaffolds under limited interaction data. The work positions linear interpretability as a viable alternative to deep architectural complexity for drug-target prediction.

papers.title: AI-Enabled Animal Behavior Analysis for Translational Pharmacology and Therapeutic Discovery.
papers.abstract: Animal behavior is a critical endpoint in preclinical pharmacology, toxicology, and therapeutic discovery, yet conventional behavioral scoring remains labor-intensive, low-dimensional, and difficult to reproduce across laboratories. Artificial intelligence (AI) can now quantify behavior from video with greater spatial, temporal, and phenotypic resolution. This review summarizes how object detection, markerless pose estimation, unsupervised behavioral segmentation, foundation models, and autonomous analysis agents are reshaping behavioral phenotyping. General-purpose object detectors rapidly lo
papers.summary: This review describes how AI methods—object detection, markerless pose estimation, unsupervised behavioral segmentation, foundation models, and autonomous analysis agents—are replacing labor-intensive manual scoring in animal behavior studies. These tools enable higher-resolution, more reproducible behavioral phenotyping for preclinical pharmacology and therapeutic discovery. The paper surveys the current landscape and likely future directions for AI-enabled behavioral analysis.

papers.title: UPLC-MS/MS-GNPS based metabolite profiling and inhibitory potential of Vitex negundo L. leaves against Shiga toxins: Applications for biodegradable films with antibacterial properties.
papers.abstract: Antibiotic therapy for STEC O157:H7 infections induces Shiga toxin release, highlighting the need for alternative, food-compatible antimicrobial strategies. The ethanolic leaf extract of Vitex negundo L. was characterized by UPLC-qTOF-MS/MS, integrated with Feature-Based Molecular Networking (GNPS), which putatively annotated 56 metabolites. Computational screening of all annotated compounds against the Stx1 and Stx2 B-subunits identified compound 8, an iridoid glycoside, as the top-ranked candidate with predicted Stx1-binding potential (ΔG = -6.9 kcal/mol; Ki = 8.7 µM). Over 100 ns of molecul
papers.summary: The study used UPLC-qTOF-MS/MS with GNPS molecular networking to annotate 56 metabolites from Vitex negundo leaf extract, then computationally screened them against Shiga toxin B-subunits, identifying an iridoid glycoside as a top Stx1 binder. The work extends toward biodegradable antibacterial films, but the abstract is truncated and the inhibitory evidence appears largely computational.

papers.title: Virology-aware artificial intelligence for respiratory antiviral discovery: from molecular docking biases to RdRp-centered benchmarking.
papers.abstract: Respiratory RNA viruses remain a persistent threat because they combine high transmissibility, rapid evolution, immune escape, zoonotic spillover, and incomplete therapeutic coverage. RNA-dependent RNA polymerases (RdRps) and polymerase complexes are among the most conserved and pharmacologically actionable viral targets, yet they are also challenging computational targets because their ligandable states depend on RNA templates, cofactors, divalent metals, multidomain architecture, and conformational transitions. Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), geometri
papers.summary: This review argues that AI-driven discovery of antivirals targeting respiratory RNA virus polymerases (RdRps) is often undermined by molecular docking biases and unrealistic target representations. The authors propose virology-aware benchmarking centered on RdRp complexes that accounts for RNA templates, metal cofactors, and conformational states. The paper is a methodological critique and roadmap rather than a primary experimental study.

papers.title: Research progress on the application of multi-scale computational methods in the research and development of anti-tuberculosis infection drugs.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), driven by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), remains a leading cause of mortality from infectious disease worldwide.​ The global dissemination of multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) strains-coupled with protracted treatment regimens and the persistence of latent infection-has not only compromised first-line chemotherapies but also underscored the stagnation of conventional drug development pipelines. In this review, we systematically synthesize how multi-scale computational strategies are reshaping anti-TB drug discovery and explicitly delineate the
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how multi-scale computational methods—spanning molecular docking, molecular dynamics, network analysis, and machine learning—are being applied to anti-tuberculosis drug discovery. It highlights how these approaches address the stagnation of conventional pipelines amid rising multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant Mtb strains, covering target identification through lead optimization.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomic and computational analysis associates Ms4a6c+ macrophages with fibrosis in radiation proctitis and computationally nominates MOTS-c as a candidate modulator.
papers.abstract: Chronic radiation proctitis (CRP) represents a significant clinical challenge characterized by irreversible fibrosis and a lack of specific pharmacological interventions. This study aimed to elucidate the cellular mechanisms underlying impaired tissue repair to identify novel therapeutic targets.
papers.summary: This study combines transcriptomic profiling with computational analyses to identify Ms4a6c+ macrophages as a cell population associated with fibrosis in chronic radiation proctitis. The authors then use computational approaches to nominate MOTS-c as a candidate modulator of this fibrotic process. The work is exploratory and hypothesis-generating, with the therapeutic candidate identified in silico rather than validated experimentally.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and anti-cancer drugs: advancing discovery, personalization, and precision oncology.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the way we discover anticancer drugs. It tackles the problems of traditional methods, such as prolonged timelines for drug development, higher costs, and substantial inter-patient heterogeneity. This review explains how AI is applied throughout the cancer drug pipeline. This includes target identification, virtual screening of compounds, molecular docking, and predicting pharmacokinetics. We explore how machine learning models speed up hit-to-lead optimization, improve clinical trial design by stratifying patients, and allow for real-time toxicity monit
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence is being applied across the anticancer drug development pipeline, from target identification and virtual screening through molecular docking, pharmacokinetic prediction, and hit-to-lead optimization. It also discusses how machine learning can improve clinical trial design via patient stratification and enable real-time toxicity monitoring, addressing traditional bottlenecks of long timelines, high costs, and inter-patient heterogeneity. As a review, it synthesizes existing approaches rather than presenting new experimental results.

papers.title: Cytochrome P450 inhibitors: friends or foes?
papers.abstract: Cytochrome P450 (CYP450) enzymes play a central role in the metabolism of xenobiotics and endogenous compounds, influencing drug pharmacokinetics, efficacy, and safety. Inhibition of these enzymes has traditionally been viewed as a major liability in drug discovery due to its association with drug-drug interactions (DDIs), toxicity, and metabolic instability. However, inhibition of specific CYP450 isoforms has emerged as a powerful therapeutic strategy in multiple disease areas, including cancer and infectious diseases. This review presents a comprehensive analysis of data and regulatory guida
papers.summary: This review argues that cytochrome P450 inhibitors, long considered a liability in drug discovery due to drug-drug interactions and toxicity, can also be exploited as therapeutic agents in cancer and infectious disease. It synthesizes data and regulatory guidance on both the risks and the therapeutic opportunities of isoform-specific CYP450 inhibition.

papers.title: Exploration or exploitation? The double-edged effects of AI use modes on radical creativity: evidence from AI-enabled drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely adopted in corporate innovation activities, yet prior research has not reached a consensus on whether it is more conducive to incremental or radical innovation. For radical innovation, which depends on highly novel ideas, realizing the value of AI depends not only on whether AI is adopted but, more importantly, on whether employees can use it creatively to transcend established knowledge boundaries. Drawing on environmental dynamism and the exploration-exploitation perspective, this study develops a theoretical model linking leaders' perceptions of
papers.summary: This study examines how different modes of AI use (exploration vs. exploitation) affect radical creativity in the context of AI-enabled drug discovery. Drawing on the exploration-exploitation framework and environmental dynamism, the authors propose a theoretical model linking leaders' perceptions to employees' creative use of AI. The work suggests that AI's impact on radical innovation depends less on adoption itself and more on how creatively employees deploy it to transcend established knowledge boundaries.

papers.title: A review on advances in chemical compound toxicology prediction.
papers.abstract: The accurate prediction of chemical toxicity remains a major challenge in drug development and chemical safety assessment because conventional approaches can be costly, time-consuming, ethically constrained, and limited in predictive performance. This review examines how artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), is being applied to predictive toxicology. It covers conventional algorithms such as support vector machines (SVMs), decision trees (DTs), and ensemble methods, together with advanced approaches including graph neural networks (GNNs). The
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning and deep learning are being applied to predict chemical toxicity, covering conventional algorithms like SVMs, decision trees, and ensembles alongside advanced graph neural networks. It highlights that AI methods offer faster, cheaper, and less ethically constrained alternatives to traditional toxicity assessment, though predictive performance remains a challenge. The paper serves as an overview of the current methodological landscape in computational toxicology.

papers.title: Integrated in vitro and in silico assessment of antimicrobial, chemical antioxidant, and cytotoxic activities of endophytic Aspergillus sp. GK1 isolated from Mentha spicata roots.
papers.abstract: Medicinal plants are a source of structurally diverse endophytic fungi which harbor significant pharmaceutical potential.
papers.summary: This study isolated the endophytic fungus Aspergillus sp. GK1 from Mentha spicata roots and characterized its antimicrobial, antioxidant, and cytotoxic activities using both in vitro assays and in silico molecular docking. The fungus showed promising antimicrobial and antioxidant effects, with chemical constituents identified that may explain these activities. The work highlights endophytic fungi from medicinal plants as a potential source of bioactive compounds for drug discovery.

papers.title: An m5C-associated NSUN5-YBX1-CENPF programme marks melanoma cell states and immune features.
papers.abstract: RNA 5-methylcytosine (m5C)-associated programmes may help characterise melanoma cell states and their immune context. We investigated an NSUN5-YBX1-CENPF (NYC) programme using patient-matched sequencing, experimental perturbation and multiscale transcriptomic analyses.
papers.summary: This study identifies an RNA m5C-associated regulatory programme—involving the methyltransferase NSUN5, the RNA-binding protein YBX1, and the target CENPF—that marks distinct melanoma cell states and correlates with immune features in patient tumours. Using matched sequencing, perturbation experiments, and multiscale transcriptomic analyses, the authors propose the NYC programme as a framework for characterising melanoma heterogeneity and its immune context.

papers.title: Plasmid-Mediated AmpC Detection in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae: In Vitro Prevalence and In Silico Inhibitor Design.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the prevalence of AmpC beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae in clinical specimens collected in Lahore, Pakistan, and aimed to identify potential inhibitors targeting AmpC beta-lactamases.
papers.journal: The Canadian journal of infectious diseases & medical microbiology = Journal canadien des maladies infectieuses et de la microbiologie medicale
papers.summary: This study screened clinical E. coli and K. pneumoniae isolates from Lahore, Pakistan for plasmid-mediated AmpC beta-lactamases, reporting their in vitro prevalence. It then used computational (in silico) approaches to design candidate inhibitor molecules targeting these AmpC enzymes.

papers.title: Investigating potential molecular mechanisms linking 6PPD-quinone exposure to Intervertebral Disc Degeneration: A network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation study.
papers.abstract: As an emerging pollutant derived from tire rubber, 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) has raised public health concerns due to widespread environmental exposure; however, its potential toxicological effects on avascular tissues such as intervertebral discs remain unclear. This study integrated network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation to investigate the potential mechanisms linking 6PPD-Q exposure to intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD). ADMET toxicological predictions indicated high model-predicted probabilities for SR-MMP and SR-ARE activation. Through multidimensio
papers.summary: This study uses computational approaches—network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation—to explore how exposure to 6PPD-quinone, an environmental pollutant from tire rubber, might contribute to intervertebral disc degeneration. The authors predict that 6PPD-Q activates stress-response pathways (SR-MMP and SR-ARE) and identify potential molecular targets linking the pollutant to disc degeneration. The work is entirely in silico and provides hypotheses rather than experimental validation.
